source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 12–18.

key_decisions.decision: Seh includes a lamb or kid as verse 5 specifies; preserves male household representative and household scale.
Preserves male age and unblemished condition, with both permitted species explicit.
Renders collective singular distributively, preserving communal slaughter; twilight represents the disputed between-the-evenings phrase.
Makes girded loins concrete as clothing preparation while retaining sandals, staff, haste, and the named rite.
Retains divine first-person agency, lethal scope and gods as the stated objects of judgment without rationalization.
Keeps the sign for the addressed people and pesach word connection; protective force explained selectively in a note.
Distinguishes leavening material from leavened food and retains cut-off sanction without choosing an unstated mechanism.
Unfolds elliptical unleavened-bread observance; retains retrospective perfect inside anticipatory speech and military-group image.
Preserves equal sanction for ger and native without softening exclusion or importing modern citizenship categories.
Retains hyssop without speculative botanical identification and takes saf as basin, noting threshold alternative.
Preserves the distinction between LORD and destroyer without adding an angel identification; doorway protection remains explicit.
Makes Pharaoh the enthroned referent and retains captive and livestock scope; no harm is euphemized.
Retains universal household death claim and collective grief without apologetic qualification.
Uses anterior action to explain departure supplies; asked does not introduce an obligation to repay.
Preserves divine favor and forceful plunder conclusion without recasting it as a loan or erasing the image.
Preserves approximate traditional number, specified males and separate dependents rather than silently recalculating population.
Follows the pinned Hebrew’s Egypt location and 430 years; does not import the longer geographical reading of other witnesses.
Maintains repeated watchfulness and LORD language without resolving the first phrase solely into divine or human vigil.
Distinguishes ben nekhar from resident foreigner admitted under verse 48, without turning the rite into an ethnic absolute.
Names purchased slavery plainly and preserves circumcision prerequisite and male pronoun.
Keeps the two excluded social categories distinct from purchased slave and circumcised ger.
Makes household scope explicit from all males belonging to him and preserves admission and exclusion together.
